nos_units.nos_title: Prepare for the Flight as a Paragliding Tandem Pilot
kus: KU1. SOPs, safety and service quality standards followed in the organization.
KU2. the company’s reporting structure and documentation procedures.
KU3. the use of safety equipment in paragliding like harness, helmet, etc.
KU4. how to check connections and fittings of the parachute and identify faulty or damaged equipment.
KU5. how to make adjustments to the Spreader Bar settings based on different pilot/student/client
KU6. how to plan and execute flights based on student’s/client’s prior experience, weather conditions and time availability.
KU7. importance of respect for students/clients, colleagues and local communities .
KU8. process of equipment and service record logbook maintenance.
gs: GS1. be prompt, punctual and organized.
GS2. plan and organize equipment checks on time.

pcs.pc_description: obtain and assess detailed information about the students’/clients’ age, gender, health issues(if any), special requests and past experience in paragliding (if any).
access and assess detailed itinerary and flight schedules from the organizer.
collate detailed equipment lists and procure paragliding gear and safety equipment based on the number of students/clients and their height/weight parameters.
ensure to check the validity of pilot and liability insurances.
ensure that the ATC and local authorities are informed about the planned route at the start of the season and before every flight day.
ensure equipment logbooks and service record books are updated and carried to the activity site.
ensure that documentation for flights with persons with disabilities has been logged and reported in advance.
ensure to brief the ground crew on the emergency action plan for the day.
ensure to inspect the condition of the Paragliding gear for self and the students/clients like tandem paraglider, harnesses, helmets, safety parachute and spreader bars.
ensure to inspect the main and reserve parachutes for appropriate connections, fittings, etc., before the flight.
access and assess detailed weather reports and decide the altitude limit for the paragliding flight.
ensure to inspect the take-off area and wind conditions for potential hazards and disturbances.
ensure that the first-aid kit is fully stocked and on the activity site.
welcome the students/clients and introduce oneself and the team in a loud, clear and friendly manner.
ensure to collect signed indemnity waivers from the students/clients and hand over to the organizer.

conduct a pre-flight briefing and demonstration for the students/clients on the use of paragliding equipment, clip in, clip out process, take-off and landing procedures, appropriate clothing for the flight, emergency procedures, etc.
brief the students/clients and make them practice essential flight communication terms and rescue signals to be followed in case emergencies.
ensure the students/clients are made aware of preexisting medical conditions that disqualify them form paragliding.
ensure to conduct a question/answer session for the students/clients addressing and clarifying all doubts before start of activity.
ensure that students/clients with asthma carry their inhalers.

nos_units.nos_title: Conduct the flight as a paragliding tandem pilot
kus: KU1. company’s SOPs on safety and service quality standards, emergency and evacuation action plans, rescue procedures and minimum impact travel and camping policies.
KU2. weather conditions, wind speeds and directions.
KU3. tandem launch and landing techniques.
KU4. the theory of flight, meteorology of flying, flying instrument reading and glider instability and
KU5. how to be polite, reassuring yet firm with the students/clients.
KU6. appropriate clothing and accessories required for the activity.
KU7. the importance of respecting persons with disabilities.
gs: GS1. manage time effectively and efficiently.
GS3. analyse and generate solutions during any crisis.

pcs.pc_description: ensure that the activity area is safe and free of all hazards.
assess and identify wind conditions for a safe launch and choose a reverse or forward launch position depending on the direction of the wind.
ensure that the student/client does not unclip from the pilot unless told to do so on command.
ensure that the launch and landing phases are well timed for a safe and steady flight.
ensure to maintain active radio communication with the crew chief informing them of all inflight developments.
ensure to check instability in a glider and make the glider horizontal by using flying instruments.
communicate all flight developments and phases to the student/client as they are about to happen like landing and launch.
assess the mental state of the student/client during the flight, ensuring to reassure the student/client in case of a panic attack or unruly behavior.
ensure that the activity is called off or cancelled if the weather and wind conditions are not ideal.
offer help to persons with disabilities, when asked for.
empathize with and respect persons with disabilities.
accommodate persons with disabilities in the activities, as far as possible, without compromising safety.
coordinate and deploy additional personnel and safety measures to cater to the requirements of persons with disabilities.
adhere to “minimum impact” policies at every level, do not burn/throw waste materials, discarded wrappers and plastic bottles into the river or any of the activity grounds.

ensure all non-biodegradable items like plastic, glass and tins are carried back to be disposed on reaching a town/city and that all leftover food/vegetables are buried in shallow pits covered with earth.
ensure not to cause damage to the fragile habitats and environments (animal life, flora and fauna) found there.

nos_units.nos_title: Conduct Post Flight Closure & Debrief as a Paragliding
kus: KU1. the manufacturer's recommended equipment maintenance policy.
KU2. proper methods of post activity equipment check and pack up.
KU3. company's documentation procedures including post trip equipment record logbook entries and equipment inspection recommendation.
KU4. the process for feedback exchange and documentation.
gs: GS1. writing equipment maintenance and service records.

modules.module_title: Pack up equipment and submit trip report

pcs.pc_description: debrief the students/clients after each flight and obtain activity evaluation and written feedback.
conduct post-flight equipment inspections and maintain a record of any damages in the equipment logbook.
maintain a detailed record of all incidents and submit trip reports and logbooks to the organizer.

nos_units.nos_title: Assess and Mitigate Risks for Paragliding Tandem Flight
kus: KU1. organisational policies and procedures to enable safe response to an emergency situation according to one's own role and level of responsibility.
KU2. contingency management techniques.
KU3. use of safety equipment, rescue techniques and wilderness first-aid methods.
KU4. the use of two-way radios for inflight communication and corresponding protocols.
KU5. how to create a detailed evacuation/emergency action plans.
KU6. communication norms for handling media.
KU7. methods for conducting risk assessment.
KU8. how to identify and avoid unfavorable winds.
gs: GS1. communicate effectively with the students/clients/team to be risk averse.
GS2. be polite but firm with the students/clients without compromising safety.
GS3. perform risk assessment of different situations.
GS4. take decisions to mitigate potential risks.
GS5. handle complicated situations in a sensitive manner.

modules.module_title: Ensure to take safety measures and respond to emergency situations

pcs.pc_description: perform a risk assessment of the activity area and ensure that it is free from hazards or disturbances before initiating the flight.
create a detailed evacuation/emergency plan to be carried out on site and brief the rest of the team on the same.
ensure that the team is aware of the emergency communication protocols between pilot and crew using two way radios and has quick access to contacts of emergency response and rescue teams.
ensure that evacuation routes are obstruction free and easily accessible.
ensure that only standardized and certified equipment is used.
access and assess the weather forecast to determine if the paragliding activity can take place and avoid strong wind and thunderstorm conditions.

verify the medical condition and the extent of students/clients ailment in person on site and ensure that students/clients with heart or spinal issues, recent surgery, epilepsy, asthma, etc., are closely monitored and pregnant ladies/underage children are not allowed to participate in the activity.
ensure that students/clients are properly attired, e.g., slippers and loose pants/pajamas should be discouraged and long hair should be tied securely before starting the activity.
ensure that nil wind launches are not attempted early and aerobatic maneuvers are not performed with the students/clients in the air.
ensure to weight the students/clients before the activity to balance the pilot/passenger weight as well as to avoid over or under loading of equipment.
ensure that the two way radio is carried for the flight and always on.
conform to the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) in Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC) guidelines and ensure that no flights are conducted at night or in cloudy conditions.

identify emergency situations and respond promptly, e.g., manage students'/clients' movement away from the emergency and provide the necessary on spot first-aid/CPR to the students/clients in case of injuries.
handle the media and family members of the injured person in a sensitive manner in case of a serious accident.
choose activity site carefully to safeguard from rockfall, flooding and lightning, etc.
evacuate students/clients from the danger zone and provide shelter till rescue arrives, in case of disasters.
establish communication and organize air and land rescue in case of any disaster.
maintain calm and be composed in an emergency situation.
